The Fourier transform describes a signal as a sum of waves. Three of its properties carry the methods of the chapters: it is a change of basis that loses nothing, it can be computed fast, and it turns every convolution into a product. We treat these in turn, then look at the price of cutting a signal into frames and at the cosine transform.

children.value: The DFT assumes that the frame repeats periodically. A tone that completes a whole number of cycles in the frame continues smoothly into the next copy, and its energy falls into a single bin. A tone with a fractional number of cycles jumps at the boundary between copies, and the jump spreads energy over all bins, the
The convolution theorem explains the effect and the cure. Cutting a frame out of a longer signal multiplies the signal with a window

children.html: w(n)w(n)w(n)

children.value: , a rectangle of ones for a plain cut. In the frequency domain, the product becomes a convolution: every spectral line is replaced by a copy of the window’s spectrum

children.html: W(k)W(k)W(k)

children.value: . The rectangle has a narrow central peak and high side lobes, which carry energy far from the true frequency. Bell-shaped windows such as Hann and Hamming fade the frame in and out, remove the jump, and have much lower side lobes, at the price of a central peak twice as wide.
Example: A tone between two bins
A tone that completes 10.5 cycles in a frame of 64 samples falls between bins 10 and 11. Without a window, the spectrum at bin 20, ten bins away, is only
dB below the peak, and at bin 30 still
dB below. With a Hamming window, the levels drop to
dB, with a Hann window to
dB. A tone with exactly 10 cycles shows no leakage even without a window.

The two windows trade differently. The Hamming window has the lowest nearest side lobe, while the side lobes of the Hann window fall off much faster with the distance, which is why it suppresses the far bins of the example better. A wider central peak blurs two tones that lie close together, a lower side lobe keeps a weak tone visible next to a strong one. Zero padding a frame before the transform samples the spectrum more densely, but it does not separate close tones: the resolution is set by the duration of the frame, as the key formula of

states. Hann windows that overlap by half their length add up to a constant, so every sample of the signal receives the same total weight over the frames; this is one reason for the hop of half a frame in many spectrograms.

children.value: , we compute the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix and the 8 DCT basis vectors. Each eigenvector has a cosine of at least
with the corresponding DCT vector, so the two bases are nearly identical. The first two principal components capture 90.1 percent of the variance, the first two DCT coefficients 89.9 percent.

The log mel energies of neighboring bands are strongly correlated, and the DCT decorrelates them almost as well as PCA would, with a fixed basis that needs no training data. Keeping the first 13 coefficients is then a dimensionality reduction that keeps most of the variance, the same reasoning as truncating a PCA.
